_description: Pre-registered Rust-gate rule for the voice relay A/B (perf-fleet P7.7). Read by tools/benchmark/rust-gate.mjs. Fix it BEFORE the first real run and never change it after seeing numbers. min_<key>: the 95% CI lower bound of the paired measurement must be >= the limit. max_<key>: the point estimate and the 95% CI upper bound must be <= the limit (a regression has to be ruled out, not merely unproven). Keys not listed here do not gate anything.

corpus._note: Seed of the byte-compare corpus (tools/voice-relay-bench/corpus.mjs). Pre-registered so a favourable corpus cannot be shopped for. The report carries the seed, the corpus SHA-256 and the libopus version.

_win_note: A candidate wins if ANY ONE of the three reductions below clears its limit (plan: UBAG-controlled overhead -20%, or CPU or RSS -25%). Reductions are paired A/B (A = optimised Python relay, B = candidate), interleaved runs, per-pair (A-B)/A. overhead = relay CPU per call-minute minus libopus self-time (the same libopus .so in A and B; the self-time comes from the P7.5 baseline profile).
_regression_note: Latency regressions are per-pair (B-A)/A for the frame transit p95 and p99, mic and speaker.
_materiality_note: Materiality in the mixed workload: the relay must be at least min_relay_share_of_container_pct of one live call's container CPU (this is also stop rule B of the P7.5 profile), and the mixed run (N mock-provider browser workloads plus one voice call, A/B interleaved) must improve container CPU, host headroom or job p95 with a CI lower bound above min_mixed_improvement_pct.
_prototype_note: Before any Rust exists the evaluator can only close the experiment or authorise a prototype: stop if libopus + syscalls hold at least stop_libopus_syscall_share_pct of relay CPU (P7.5 rule A) or the relay is under min_relay_share_of_container_pct of the container (rule B); a prototype is authorised only if the Python-owned overhead (relay CPU outside libopus and syscalls) is at least min_python_overhead_share_pct of relay CPU. That is necessary, never sufficient.
